To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a) local correlation methods can be used to study metal-metal bonding, and b) ligand effects are important in determining the strength of metal-metal bonds.
aurophilic complexes can exhibit a variety of interactions and the ligand environment can have a strong impact on the metal-metal interaction.
the metal-metal interaction in Au(I) dimers can be separated from ligand interactions through local correlation methods, and the resulting energy profile is independent of ligand identity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the ligand effects on the aurophilic interaction in a series of Au(I) dimers.
the development of a new tool for the analysis of metal-metal interactions in d(10) systems.
the development of a methodology which is able to separate the metal-metal interactions from the ligand-ligand interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metal-metal interaction in Au(I) dimers is dominated by ligand effects, which can be separated by the use of local correlations and orbital populations.
the interaction energy is a function of the ligand and metal-metal distance and the ligand effects are more pronounced than the metal-metal interactions.
aurophilic and other d(10)-metal d(10)-interactions should be considered as a sum of several contributions and that the metal-metal bond is not always the dominant factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metallophilic interactions in the complexes studied here are dominated by ligand effects and not metal-metal interactions.
aurophilicity is not the only driving force for d(10)- d(10) interactions.
aurophilicity is not the only factor that drives dimer formation and the role of ligand effects should not be underestimated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metal-metal bond is not always the strongest interaction in play.
the ligand effects can be significant in the interaction energy of the metallocomplexes.
the ligands can have a strong impact on the d(10)- d(10) interaction energy and that the use of local methods is essential to properly separate this contribution.
